strengths: Clear problem motivation addressing real limitations of existing extrapolative NVS methods
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Co3D, DTU, RealEstate10K) with appropriate baselines and both interpolative and extrapolative settings
Strong empirical results showing state-of-the-art performance on extrapolative view synthesis with good zero-shot generalization
Well-motivated cross-modal attention distillation mechanism with clear visual justification (Figure 3)
Flexible architecture that generalizes to variable numbers of input views despite 2-view training
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component
Practical technical contributions including proximity-based mesh conditioning and camera-space coordinate normalization

No computational cost analysis provided (training time, inference time, memory requirements) despite training on 3 large datasets

Missing comparison with relevant method CAT3D [6] despite inclusion in references; limited analysis of failure modes and scene type limitations

Limited novelty in individual components (warping-and-inpainting from prior work, geometry conditioning established by GenWarp); main novelty is cross-modal attention which shows modest improvement (~0.03 LPIPS)
Geometry evaluation primarily via depth metrics rather than 3D reconstruction quality; no comparison with dedicated depth prediction methods or standard 3D benchmarks

Comprehensive experimental evaluation on multiple datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) with zero-shot generalization
Clear intuition for cross-modal distillation with good visualization of per-modality attention differences (Figure 3)
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component

Good qualitative results with reasonable geometric alignment in point cloud visualizations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: warping-and-inpainting [5,25], aggregated attention [9,25], and attention-map transfer are relatively straightforward combinations of existing ideas

Incomplete experimental results: Table 5 (depth prediction accuracy) marked as 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled'—unacceptable for conference submission
Insufficient analysis of core contribution: why transfer only attention maps? Why asymmetric design in Eq. 7? Missing ablation on when distillation occurs (training vs. inference)
Critical details relegated to appendix: camera-space pointmap normalization is essential (Figure 9) but treated as supplementary; should be in main paper
Limited geometry evaluation: only depth metrics (Abs.Rel, δ1.25), no 3D evaluation (Chamfer distance, F-score) or mesh quality assessment

strengths: Well-motivated core contribution: The observation that geometry completion is more deterministic than image inpainting is insightful, and cross-modal attention distillation is an elegant solution to the alignment problem

Comprehensive experimental validation: Consistent improvements across three datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D), both interpolative and extrapolative settings, zero-shot generalization, and thorough ablations demonstrating each component's contribution

Coherent technical framework: Multiple components (multi-view aggregated attention, pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, cross-modal distillation) are well-integrated into a unified system
Practical advantages: Works with unposed reference images, produces aligned 3D geometry, requires no per-scene optimization, and achieves strong results in challenging extrapolative scenarios
Clear presentation: Well-organized paper with effective visualizations, particularly Figures 2 and 3, that clearly convey the architecture and motivation for core contributions
weaknesses: Critical incompleteness: Table 5 (depth prediction accuracy) is marked 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled' - unacceptable for a conference submission and undermines confidence in geometry evaluation claims

Limited core novelty: Warping-and-inpainting framework is from prior work; cross-modal attention mechanism (Eq. 7) is straightforward (just replacing K,Q); no thorough justification for why this specific design choice (excluding V transfer) is optimal

Heavy dependence on external VGGT geometry predictor: Method quality ceiling limited by VGGT; no ablation across different geometry predictors; unclear how much improvement comes from better VGGT utilization vs. algorithmic contributions; VGGT is concurrent work (2025) raising reproducibility concerns

Insufficient geometry evaluation: Geometry mostly evaluated qualitatively; limited quantitative metrics; no comparison against 3D ground truth benchmarks; depth prediction ablations relegated to appendix or incomplete

Insufficient technical analysis: Cross-modal attention mechanism lacks thorough justification; claim about preventing 'harmful mixing' needs stronger support; no systematic ablation of alternative cross-modal designs; limited analysis of when/why the mechanism fails
Unclear positioning on pose-requirement: Claims 'unposed' images but requires camera poses from VGGT; should clarify this differs from truly pose-free methods

Incomplete comparisons: LVSM comparison only qualitative (Fig. 7); SV3D [27] cited but not compared; missing comparisons with other recent methods; no quantitative benchmarks on shared evaluation protocols

strengths: Well-motivated pose-free novel view synthesis problem with clear practical applications and elegant solution to ensure image-geometry alignment
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) with both zero-shot and in-domain evaluation, including extensive ablations and robustness tests
Strong empirical results, particularly for extrapolative view synthesis (SOTA in extrapolation: 17.41 PSNR vs 14.36 for NoPoSplat), with efficient inference (9.67s vs 209.19s for ViewCrafter)
Clear technical contributions including cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI), proximity-based mesh conditioning, and camera-space normalization, each with demonstrated benefits
Excellent reproducibility emphasis with detailed implementation details, promised code/weights release, and strong documentation of methods and hyperparameters
Good architectural design enabling variable input views, image-only inference mode, and geometric alignment without scale-shift fitting
weaknesses: Limited core novelty—primarily engineering contribution building incrementally on well-established warping-and-inpainting methods (LucidDreamer, GenWarp); MoAI's core mechanism (attention map swapping) is conceptually simple without deeper theoretical insight

Heavy dependency on external VGGT geometry predictor limits novelty scope; essentially a wrapper combining existing components; 'pose-free' claim is somewhat misleading as poses are still estimated externally
Insufficient analysis of why MoAI works beyond intuitive Fig. 3 motivation; lacks investigation of alternative designs (reverse instillation, partial transfer); mechanism appears somewhat heuristic

Significant geometry evaluation gaps: lacks quantitative metrics (depth accuracy, point cloud errors) on standard benchmarks; evaluation primarily visual; no comparison of geometry quality to depth-focused methods or user studies validating alignment
Conservative extrapolation evaluation with limited systematic analysis of extreme view differences; no discussion of failure modes or scene types where method struggles
Critical implementation detail (camera-space pointmap normalization) buried in appendix despite Fig. 8 showing substantial performance impact; should be elevated to main paper
Scalability concerns: training with batch size 1, 28GB memory for joint generation, unclear how method scales to higher resolutions or larger-scale scenes

Limited generalization analysis: evaluation concentrated on indoor/object-centric scenes; minimal outdoor and large-scale evaluation; no systematic analysis of challenging scenarios (transparency, thin structures, dynamic content)

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive quantitative benchmarks, zero-shot generalization tests, and robustness analysis demonstrating competitive empirical results
Well-motivated problem addressing the gap between interpolation-capable and extrapolation-capable NVS methods with practical pose-free setting
Strong computational efficiency (9.67s inference) and demonstrated generalization to unseen data with detailed ablations and implementation transparency
Practical flexibility supporting variable input views and joint image-geometry synthesis with visually plausible results
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: warping-and-inpainting and diffusion-based NVS are well-established; the main contribution (MoAI) reduces to sharing attention maps without sufficient justification for why this specific design is optimal over alternatives

Insufficient analysis of Cross-Modal Attention Instillation: motivation relies on anecdotal single-example (wheel) with no ablation on bidirectional sharing, alternative feature-sharing strategies, or experimental evidence that attention-map-only avoids feature mixing

Circular evaluation protocol undermines geometric claims: ground truth geometry obtained by applying VGGT to target images means the model learns VGGT consistency, not true geometric accuracy; geometric metrics measure VGGT prediction matching rather than real accuracy

Heavy unexplored dependency on external VGGT model for pose estimation and geometric conditioning; while noise robustness is tested, failure modes and comparison with other predictors are not addressed

Insufficient geometric evaluation: no quantitative depth/normal consistency metrics, all evaluation is visual; claims of 'geometrically aligned' point clouds lack rigorous validation; no analysis of physical consistency
Experimental design concerns: batch size 1 risks batch norm instability, modest ablation gains for MoAI (0.86 dB), perturbation robustness shows meaningful degradation (-2.45 dB at 15% noise)

Critical details hidden in appendix (camera-space normalization significantly impacts results); proximity-based mesh conditioning adds complexity without isolated ablation; normal masking threshold appears arbitrary

strengths: Well-motivated cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI) mechanism with genuine insight into complementary image/geometry behaviors, validated by clear visual evidence (Fig. 3)
Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art on extrapolative view synthesis (PSNR: 17.41 vs 14.36 for next best on RealEstate10K) across multiple benchmarks
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations, robustness analysis, and diverse baselines (feedforward, warping-inpainting, large models) across multiple datasets
Practical pose-free framework using off-the-shelf geometry predictors with proven robustness to noise/sparsity and cross-predictor compatibility
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementation details, promised code/weights release, good hyperparameter documentation, and clear architectural specifications
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components—warping-and-inpainting is established prior work, ball-pivoting is standard, main contribution reduces to applying existing inpainting to geometry plus attention map swapping, making overall contribution incremental

Incomplete geometric evaluation—quantitative geometry metrics (Abs.Rel, δ1.25) relegated to Table 4 without baseline comparisons; missing standard 3D metrics (Chamfer distance, volumetric IoU); geometry visualized as heatmaps not interpretable point clouds

Unclear scale-shift resolution mechanism—paper claims solving scale-shift by 'generating as continuation' but the technical details and guarantees are vague; unclear how well this works for scenes with extreme depth variation

Evaluation fairness concerns—zero-shot DTU evaluation fine-tunes on RealEstate10K/Co3D/MVImgNet (potential unfair advantage); different datasets used for different comparisons; missing quantitative metrics against large model baselines (LVSM, ViewCrafter) on identical splits

Limited failure case analysis—no discussion of when method struggles, which scene types are problematic, how extreme extrapolation (>90°) is handled, or robustness to reflections/occlusions; missing user studies for perceptual quality

Technical presentation issues—MoAI mechanism presented abstractly before implementation details; crucial camera-space normalization (Fig. 8 shows major impact) relegated to appendix; scale-shift mechanism poorly explained; limited justification for design choices

Computational overhead not fully quantified—28GB memory and 9.67s inference slower than feedforward methods; training efficiency with batch size 1 not discussed; practical applicability costs underexplored

Narrow experimental scope—primarily object-centric/indoor scenes (Co3D, RealEstate10K); large-scale outdoor evaluation limited (in-the-wild results only qualitative in appendix); unclear generalization to unconstrained real-world data
